questions.question: How does the brightness of two bulbs connected in parallel compare to the same two bulbs connected in series, using the same battery?
options: The bulbs in parallel are dimmer than the bulbs in series.
The bulbs in parallel are brighter than the bulbs in series.
The bulbs in parallel have the exact same brightness as the bulbs in series.
The bulbs in parallel do not light up at all, while the series ones do.

questions.question: When comparing two bulbs in parallel to two bulbs in series with the same battery, what is true about the current through them?
options: The current through the parallel bulbs is smaller than through the series bulbs.
No current flows through the parallel bulbs, only through the series bulbs.
The current through the parallel bulbs is bigger than through the series bulbs.
The current through both circuits is exactly the same.

questions.question: If you have two circuits, one with two bulbs in parallel and another with two bulbs in series connected to identical batteries, what will happen to the batteries?
options: The battery lighting the parallel circuit will run out faster.
The battery lighting the series circuit will run out faster.
Both batteries will run out at exactly the same time.
Neither battery will ever run out because the bulbs share the voltage.

questions.question: In physics, what is the definition of electrical resistance?
options: A measure of the total amount of energy stored in a battery.
A measure of how difficult it is for an electric current to flow.
The speed at which electrons travel around a closed loop.
The total number of electrons present in a wire.

questions.question: How does the length of a wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: The longer the wire, the greater its resistance.
The longer the wire, the smaller its resistance.
The length of a wire has no effect on its resistance.
A longer wire only has resistance if it is coiled.

questions.question: If you double the length of a piece of uniform wire, what happens to its resistance?
options: The resistance is halved.
The resistance remains unchanged.
The resistance doubles.
The resistance becomes four times greater.

questions.question: Which statement describes the relationship between the resistance of a uniform wire and its length?
options: The resistance of a wire is proportional to its length.
The resistance of a wire is inversely proportional to its length.
The resistance of a wire is equal to the square of its length.
There is no mathematical relationship between resistance and length.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, what is each individual loop equivalent to when connected to the same battery?
options: A series circuit connected to the same battery.
A short circuit that bypasses the battery completely.
An open circuit with infinitely high resistance.
An electrostatic field with no current flow.

questions.question: What does the electrical power of a device measure?
options: The total quantity of charge stored within the device.
The amount of energy used by or supplied to the device in one second.
The maximum current that can flow through the device without damaging it.
The total electrical resistance of the device's internal components.

questions.question: What is the unit used to measure electrical power?
options: Joules (J)
Ohms (Ω)
Amps (A)
Watts (W)

questions.question: How can you calculate the energy used by an electrical device in kilowatt-hours (kWh)?
options: Divide the power in watts by the time in seconds.
Multiply the power in kilowatts (kW) by the time in hours (h).
Multiply the current in amps by the resistance in ohms.
Divide the voltage in volts by the power in kilowatts.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines a parallel circuit?
options: A circuit that has only one continuous pathway from one end of a battery to the other.
A circuit with more than one complete loop, from one end of a battery to the other end.
A circuit that only contains voltmeters and no bulbs or resistors.
A circuit that is completely disconnected so that no current can flow.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, how does the current in the individual branches relate to the total current through the battery?
options: The current through each branch is always double the total current through the battery.
The current through each branch adds up to the total current through the battery.
The current through each branch is completely independent and has no relation to the battery current.
The current through the battery is divided by the number of branches squared.

questions.question: How does the thickness of a wire affect its electrical resistance?
options: The thicker the wire, the smaller its resistance.
The thicker the wire, the greater its resistance.
Thickness has no effect on resistance, only the length of the wire does.
A thicker wire has zero resistance regardless of its material.

questions.question: What happens to the resistance of a wire if its cross-sectional area is doubled?
options: The resistance doubles.
The resistance halves.
The resistance remains exactly the same.
The resistance decreases to one-quarter of its original value.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, how does the voltage across each branch compare to the voltage across the cell or battery?
options: The voltage across each branch is the same as the voltage across the cell or battery.
The voltage across each branch is divided by the number of branches in the circuit.
The voltage across each branch is always zero.
The voltage across each branch is doubled compared to the battery voltage.
